title: Decoder floors, case (b) for every number of terms: one-sided P112 decoders cost ≥ 64 without corrections (unique optimum) and with ≤ 2 non-full corrections (no κ claim)
body:
**Status: research note with exact finite computations and written proofs (not a SAT/DRAT proof). No κ claim, no supplier word.** Only `research/one-sided-decoders-all-m/` is added; nothing existing is changed.

## What this proves (scope is the claim)

Model of #2338 / #2277 / #2724 / #1224: exact masked decoders `N = Σ_{j≤m} p_j q_jᵀ` of the **Gram realisation** of the P112 pattern, field of **characteristic 0**, dense pairing table `B`, cost `Σ_j rank_F2 B[R_j, A_j]`. **Case (b): one factor outside `col M`** (the other in `col M`), **every number of terms `m`**. Reduced to the `(y, U)` form; the decoder is a lift `S ⊇ 𝒞` of the root code, `cost ≥ cost_w(S)` (min-weight basis).

* **R1 (CHECKED + PROVEN).** ε-free one-sided P112 decoders cost **≥ 64 for every `d = dim(𝒞 ∩ S_{≤7})`**: exact DP for `d ≤ 6`, an LP with exact integer dual certificates for `d = 7, 8` (`lp3.py`), re-derived by an independent symmetrised LP with exact rational duals (`symlp.py`); the multiset enumeration is complete (`enum.py`: none for `d ≤ 6`, one at `d = 7`, seven at `d = 8`, all killed).
* **R2 (Theorem U′).** The cost-64 ε-free decoder is **unique**: the coordinate decoder (8 terms `(e_j, W_j)`). Cost-65 decoders have at most one non-full correction; the cost-66 case is reduced to six OPEN `d = 8` weight multisets.
* **R3 (corrections).** Lemma P: a *full* corrected term (`U = F2⁹`) is absorbed at no cost. **Corrected cost ≥ 64 whenever at most 2 corrected terms of the normalised decoder are non-full** (normalise = merge proportional corrected terms and absorb full ones, repeated until stable; terminates since (#terms, #full corrected) drops lexicographically; the version for raw decoders is the lift-level form R4 with `I` = all corrected terms); in general `≥ 64 − max(0, n_nf − 2) ≥ 58`. The **root-swap family attains 64 exactly** with `n_nf = 1, 2, 3, 4` (exact `P·Y = C`), so `Δ ≥ n_nf` is tight.
* **R4 (lift level).** Every `S ⊇ 𝒞_{X_I}` has `cost_w(S) ≥ 64 + min(|I|, 2)`; every lift of the E8 root code has `cost_w ≥ 66`.
* **R5.** Lemma N (≤ 2 directions per 7-flat after removing ≤ 4 lines; exact counts for `|L| = 1, 2`, an upper bound for `|L| ≤ 4`, and an independent C implementation) and the Pencil Lemma (`d ≤ 2`).
* Gain-law reading (philippeVV, Discussion #1587 follow-up 6): in this class the gain on P112 is at most 48 (`112 − 64`).

## Open residue (stated exactly, not claimed)

`Δ ≥ n_nf` for `n_nf ≥ 3`: at `n_nf = 3` exactly six `d = 8` multisets of the weight-≤7 basis remain (`[7^5,6^5,1]`, `[7^6,6^4]`, `[7^8,5,4,1]`, `[7^8,5,5]`, `[7^8,6,3,1]`, `[7^8,6,4]`). Not claimed here.

## Not covered (stated up front)

* Case (c) (rank-9 realisations, see #2784), two-sided decoders, P104 and other units, `B` of rank ≥ 10, positive characteristic.
* **Imported (merged results, not re-derived):** Gram realisation (#1212 Theorem 1, plus a diagonal normalisation); dense table (#2338 Theorem R, DRAT-checked there). The parabolic-flat fact is proved in the README (C3).
* Not DRAT / Lean: written proofs plus exact Python/C computations, re-runnable.

## Labels and verification

PROVEN / CHECKED / RECORDED / IMPORTED / OPEN per claim in the README. `bash verify.sh` (about 12–15 minutes, two processes, no SAT) re-runs every exact check (DP, enumeration, LP certificates, Lemma N in two implementations, the root-swap family) and asserts them in `checks/check_logs.py`; fresh `git archive` export: 34 PASS / 0 FAIL in 714 s (logs in `evidence/logs`).

## Overlap

Scanned the 1,000 most recent PRs (titles), 119 decoder-related bodies and 100 recent Discussions: no ε-free one-sided floor for all `m`, LP/charging certificates, uniqueness statement, root-swap family or Lemma N. Nearest: #1224 (model), #1180 (both factors in the root code), #1633, #1815, #1609, and our #2338 / #2277 / #2724 (this is the every-`m` extension of #2724's case (b) at `m = 9`, by a different method).
